Trialed Devin, it's quite impressive when it understands code formatting and local test setup, but it always adds extraneous changes beyond the task that can break other things, and can't undo those changes if asked. Recommending cancelling it because it's not actually saving time and it's quite expensive.
One thing that surprised me is there doesn't seem to be an 'ask for help' escape hatch in Devin - it would work away for literally days on a task where any human would admit they were stuck.
Devin does ask for help when it can't do something, but it really hates asking for help if it's a skill issue - it would prefer running in circles than admitting it just can't do something.
You can set a 'max work time' before Devin pauses so it won't go for days endlessly spending your credits. By default it's set to 10 credits.

I've learned to just click 'Terminate Session' immediately after spotting Devin doing something hopeless. I've managed to get real work done out of it without much effort, just checking every 10-15 minutes and typing a few lines or restarting session.
Between when Cognition showed their Devin demo last June and what I'm hearing now, the product has not evolved in a way where they are providing value commensurate with their marketing or hype.
The Devin name/branding is so toxic that nobody will try their current product offerings.
